details:
@aerodrome-finance/contracts namesquats Aerodrome Finance, a real DeFi protocol on Base, under a scope with no relation to the project's actual GitHub org or any legitimate npm publication. Version 1.0.0 ships a `preinstall`/`postinstall` hook (`node index.js || true`) that runs automatically on `npm install`.

index.js scans `process.env` for any variable whose name matches a broad credential regex (KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, PRIVATE, MNEMONIC, RPC, AWS, GITHUB, NPM, KUBE, VAULT, AUTH, PGP, GPG, SEED, WALLET), reads `~/.npmrc` and `~/.gitconfig`, and lists the contents of `~/.ssh`, `~/.foundry/keystores`, `~/.config/hardhat`, and `~/.config/gcloud` — directories that hold SSH keys, Foundry/Hardhat wallet keystores, and GCP credentials respectively. It bundles the harvested data (hostname, username, cwd, platform, env vars, file contents, directory listings) into a single JSON payload and POSTs it over HTTPS to an attacker-controlled webhook.site endpoint. The install script is wrapped in a bare try/catch so it never breaks the install regardless of outcome, keeping the exfiltration silent.

This package is one of six published from the same npm account within a ~20 second window on 2026-08-11 (05:41-06:08 UTC), all namesquatting real DeFi protocols (Euler's EVC, Aerodrome Finance, Camelot AMM, and the boring-vault pattern) and all shipping a byte-identical credential-harvesting template that differs only in the `pkg` field logged in the exfiltrated JSON and the destination `raw TCP connect` IP for the same webhook.site host. Two further packages from the same actor and same webhook.site path (PyPI `dlmm` and `dlmm-sdk`, namesquatting Meteora's DLMM SDK) were also sandbox-confirmed running the equivalent harvester but have since been removed from PyPI.

Any environment where this package was installed should be treated as having had its environment variables, `.npmrc`, `.gitconfig`, and any present SSH/Foundry/Hardhat/gcloud credentials exposed to the attacker; rotate all reachable secrets, especially npm publish tokens and any wallet/RPC keys.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
